source_title: Dido, Reflective Hell, and Virgil's Embarrassment
summary: This June 21, 2026 Dante livestream extends existing Guide Trap, Eschatology, Poetry, Stories, and Fictional Heroes pressure: hell becomes a mirror for sin, Virgil's authority stops at inner hell, and literature can move desire from fantasy into action.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Dante names Dido to restore the person Virgil's silence would leave buried.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The episode read already links this exact mark to the public Guide Trap memory-repair anchor; the new source confirms the April 8 Dido mechanism rather than requiring a new Dido page.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: A guide may be necessary, intimate, and authoritative, yet still be unable to complete the journey he began.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The read already links this guide limitation to the existing necessary-guide anchor; the source sharpens the mechanism through Dis and Virgil's embarrassed pride.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Virgil can rule outer hell and teach its grammar, but the guide's world must still be overcome inside the reader.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This belongs to Fictional Heroes and Guide Trap as the interior-guide mechanism, not to a standalone Virgil's Jurisdiction topic page.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use in a future Guide Trap replacement or compression pass: the city of Dis shows Virgil as master of outer hell but not inner hell, and his pride becomes visible when divine intervention has to open what his infernal expertise cannot.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Guide Trap owns trusted mediation, Virgil's local authority, and the moment when the guide's world cannot open the next gate. Eschatology owns hell as final-order world; Fictional Heroes owns the guide as an interior literary presence.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold for a future Eschatology or Dante-hell replacement pass: infernal punishment is reflective or redemptive justice, not arbitrary torment, because it mirrors the inner structure of lust, gluttony, greed, and wrath back to the sinner.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Eschatology owns hell as a world and justice form. Free Will owns the recognition-and-choice side if the emphasis becomes conversion or agency; Guide Trap owns Virgil's authority within that world.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only if a future Free Will pass needs the recognition layer: hell's mirror is redemptive only if the sinner can recognize error and choose differently, so punishment is not pure vengeance.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Free Will should not absorb all reflective-hell material. It owns agency, recognition, and noncoercion; Eschatology owns infernal architecture.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use in a future Poetry or Stories pass: Francesca's Lancelot reading is a compact scene where literature is not decorative but causal, moving desire from fantasy into embodied action and catastrophe.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Poetry owns the medium by which language enters memory and remakes conduct. Stories owns reality-control when the emphasis is narrative machinery; Love owns the love/lust distinction only when recognition of the other person is primary.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only as comparison pressure for story-as-causal-force: the book of Lancelot functions as the hinge that converts imagination and desire into a decision with real consequences.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Stories should not become a generic literature page. Route this source there only if the future synthesis centers how narrative scripts control action rather than the poetic medium itself.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use as confirmation for Virgil as dangerous interior guide: the June 21 source adds the outer/inner hell jurisdiction line and the guide's embarrassed pride to the existing interior-guide anchor.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Fictional Heroes owns the interior literary presence. Guide Trap owns the mediation failure; Poetry owns the medium that lets the guide enter the self.

new_lens_seeds.title: Reflective Justice
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Punishment becomes just when it mirrors the inner form of the sin back to the sinner, forcing recognition rather than merely inflicting pain.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism can compare Dante's lust, gluttony, greed, wrath, chosen hell, and later self-redemption material; it also gives a diagnostic for institutions that claim to reform by making people see the shape of their own disorder.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed. It is strong enough to track, but a public page would be premature until the Dante hell cluster shows whether this should be an Eschatology section, a Free Will submechanism, or a child concept.

new_lens_seeds.title: Hell Has No Unity
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Sinful or infernal worlds become factional and territorial because ego prevents common purpose; even members of the same world gatekeep and fight one another.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The formulation can bridge Dis, Italian factionalism, gatekeeping, and political fragmentation, but the current source uses it as a Dante-world diagnosis rather than a mature public political lens.
new_lens_seeds.boundary_note: Hold as a seed. Do not turn one Dis discussion into a standalone politics page; route by active mechanism if later sources repeat factional hell.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2026-06-21, this livestream comes after the April 8 guide-trap foundation and the April 29 hierarchy-of-hell source: it confirms Dido memory repair, then adds the Dis jurisdiction layer where Virgil is master of outer hell but not inner hell.
This source is the clearest current formulation of reflective or redemptive infernal justice: hell's punishments put a mirror to the sinner's face rather than operating as pure vengeance.
The Francesca section gives a later Dante classroom example of literature as causal action: a romance text helps move desire from fantasy into embodiment and then into catastrophe.

next_actions.action: Do not create standalone Dido, Francesca, Reflective Justice, Redemptive Justice, Gluttony, Greed, Dis, Inner Hell, Outer Hell, Hell Has No Unity, or Virgil's Embarrassment pages from this source alone.

If public synthesis follows, prefer a Dante-cluster replacement/compression pass on Guide Trap or Eschatology rather than an ordinary append; both pages are below hard split pressure but already dense enough that new Dante evidence should replace, route, or seed.
No immediate episode-to-lens repair is required for the strongest Guide Trap marks: the read already links Dido memory repair, necessary-guide danger, and Virgil as interior guide to stable anchors.

If the reflective-justice seed recurs in later Dante or non-Dante sources, compare it against Eschatology, Free Will, and Guide Trap before promotion; the promotion question is whether the active mechanism is final-order architecture, free recognition, or guided passage through hell.
